title: Costa Rica Stone Spheres Puzzle

scenes.text: Hundreds of perfectly round stones, from 5 cm to 2 m, dot a jungle valley.
The spheres range from 5 cm to 2 m in diameter and were carved from local granodiorite.
Early 20th‑century photograph taken by archaeologist Samuel Kirkland Lothrop.

scenes.label: STATUS SYMBOLS
scenes.sub: Possibly markers of power or astronomy.
scenes.text: Current theories link them to status symbols of the extinct Diquís culture.
Follow if the unknown keeps you up at night.

description: The mysterious stone spheres of Costa Rica are flawless, varied, and still unexplained. Explore the facts, the leading theories, and the ongoing research.
